_what: Frozen evidence for ADR-010 Decision 2: the five ids POST /tasks accepts (the incumbent default first, then the four the M9 ablation runs), as https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models returned them.
_why_refrozen: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` — the model that DEFINES the owner's price ceiling — moved from 0.00000144/0.00000288 to 0.0000016/0.0000032 per token inside a single working session. Caught by review round 3 (PR #15, R16) comparing this file against the live endpoint. The other four entries were unchanged to the digit and _total_models_in_response was 414 in both reads, so this is real supplier drift, not a transcription error — and it is the strongest possible argument for the snapshot existing at all: a list price quoted in prose goes stale in hours.
_ceiling_rule: The owner's ruling (2026-08-20) is that the CEILING IS THE MODEL, NOT THE NUMBER: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` stays in the ablation set at whatever it lists for, and every other ablated model must price at or under it on both prompt and completion. `planner.CEILING_MODEL` names it; the effective ceiling is derived from this file's entry for it, so a number here and a number in code can no longer disagree.
_selection_source: https://openrouter.ai/rankings#leaderboard-table, 'Usage data through Aug 19, 2026'. That page states: 'These rankings measure adoption, not quality. They do not rank models by accuracy, reasoning ability, or benchmark performance' — verified first-hand. The rank positions in ADR-010 come from the coordinating session's in-app browser read; the table itself is script-rendered and not readable here.
